SMT . JUSTICE

LALITHA KANNEGANTI  ORAL JUDGMENT Aggrieved by the order passed in M.V.C.No.325/2020 dated 18.07.2022 by the Principle Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III, Chitradurga, the appellant/claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-III, Chitradurga
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition is filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.21,50,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.

The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.4,48,094/-.
2.

It is the case of the claimant that on 26.06.2019 at about 10:00 a.m., when the claimant was proceeding on his motorbike from Challakere Circle towards Guilalu, at that time NC:
2025:KHC:24790 HC-KAR the driver of the tractor-trailer drove his tractor from industrial area to N.H.4 road, in a rash and negligent manner and hit the bike of the claimant and caused accident.
Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained injuries all over the body.
Immediately, he was shifted to the hospital and was treated as inpatient.
3. It is the evidence of the doctor that the claimant had sustained 89% of disability to the whole body and the claimant was doing agricultural work as well as real estate business.

The Court has not Smt C M Sulaiman Shariff vs Shrirama General Insurance Co Ltd on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199462321/
2 considered the future loss of earnings on the ground that the petitioner even after the accident is continuing to do the agricultural and real estate business.

sentences.text:
When it comes to the pain and suffering,
the Court had awarded an amount of Rs.50,000/- and a sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during laid up period, an amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness and an amount of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards diet and other charges and towards medical expenses
an amount of Rs.3,33,094/- is awarded.
NC: 2025:KHC:24790 HC-KAR 4.

Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the Tribunal had not awarded reasonable compensation for the injuries sustained by the claimant when the claimant has sustained whole body disability of 26%.
The Court is not right in granting the loss of future earnings.
Learned counsel submits that the Court ought to have taken the income at Rs.14,000/- p.m. as the accident is of the year 2019.
He submits that the compensation needs to be enhanced.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the claimant was working even after the accident and as there is no impact on his future income, the Court is granted an amount of not considered the future loss of income and the amount that is granted by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
6. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the entire material on record.
Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant

, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.60,000/-
under the head pain and suffering.

Coming to the loss of income during laid up period, as there is no evidence on record, as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State NC: 2025:KHC:24790 HC-KAR Legal Services Authority, as this is an accident of the year 2019, this Court is taking the income at Rs.14,000/-p.m., for three months he is entitled for an amount of Rs.42,000/- under the head loss of income laid up period.

Considering 89% of limb disability, this Court has taken whole body disability at 26%, then the loss of future income comes to Rs.6,55,200/-
(Rs.14,000X12X15X26%).
The Court below had granted Rs.25,000/- towards diet and other charges and this Court is not inclined to interfere with the same.
The Court had granted medical expenses at Rs.3,33,094/- as per the evidence and no interference is called for.

Then towards loss of amenities,
the Court had granted an amount of Rs.25,000/-, considering the disability, this Court is granting an amount of Rs.50,000/-.

7. The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
SL. Heads Compensation Compensation No. Awarded by Awarded by Tribunal this Court 1. Injury pain and : Rs. 50,000/- 60,000/-
sufferings 2. Loss of income : Rs. 15,000/- 42,000/-

6. Loss of amenities : Rs. 25,000/- 50,000/-
8. Altogether the claimant is entitled for compensation of an amount of Rs.11,65,294/-.
9. Accordingly, the appeal of the claimant is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation from an amount of Rs.4,48,094/- to Rs.11,65,294/-.
i) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
ii) The respondent No.1-Insurance Company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.

On such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
